GROWTH, and the reason the S11 seam was worth cutting. THE guarantee -- every ALLOW is a write the tree question positively placed inside a worktree, or an invocation no gate was deployed for -- has twice been asserted in prose and been false (CLAUDE.md 7; issue #4), and settling it both times meant a person reading every return in GateHook by hand. This enumerates the input matrix instead: 7 lane arguments x 5 ticket arguments x 7 stdins (including a real BOM, a NotebookEdit payload, empty, and a throwing read) x 4 daemon answers. Seen RED under all three s-gate mutants, each of which is a real unchecked allow.

GROWTH over Cli.ParseArgs, the other half of seam S11. `orphans` was missing from boolFlags, so a flag not in that set registers only when another argument FOLLOWS it -- and as the last word on the line it fell through to the positional list. `stop-all --orphans` therefore did nothing at all for as long as the flag existed, and the only way anyone found out was by running it.

GROWTH over Cli.ParseArgs. --root NAMES a path and --adopt is what turns naming one into taking it on (issue #12, the MassWorks adoption). The flags may be written in either order and must mean the same thing, which is why the promotion is resolved after the parse loop rather than inside it; and without --adopt a typed --root stays NAMED, which is the whole distinction.
